notes.text: Overall: This is a deliberately flawed fixture repository seeded with vulnerabilities (command injection, SQL injection, eval RCE, hardcoded secrets, XSS sinks, bare except, etc.) and code-quality issues (massive duplication, dead code, import cycles, missing lockfile). The static analysis findings are largely accurate except for the two 'secrets' findings which are redacted placeholders. The legacy-monolith.js is the largest debt hotspot — 60 copy-pasted handlers with a logic bug in every one. The Python auth module has critical RCE via eval and silent exception swallowing. The TypeScript payment module has SQL injection and eval. The Express entry point has command injection, hardcoded admin secret, sequential awaits, and HTML injection. Dependency hygiene is poor (latest, *, left-pad, no lockfile). Architecture shows an import cycle (a.js↔b.js) and several orphan modules. No test files present. Recommend prioritizing: 1) Remove eval/child_process injection sinks, 2) Fix SQL injection, 3) Eliminate hardcoded secrets, 4) Refactor legacy-monolith, 5) Add lockfile and pin dependencies.

findings.title: Massive copy-paste duplication in legacy-monolith.js — 60 near-identical handlers
findings.description: 60 handler functions (handler0–handler59) are copy-pasted with only the numeric suffix changed. This inflates the file to 1,330 lines, makes maintenance error-prone, and indicates a missing abstraction (e.g., a factory function or router).
findings.suggestion: Replace with a single parameterized handler factory: `function makeHandler(prefix) { return (req, res) => { … } }` and register routes programmatically.
findings.benefit: Reduces file size by ~95%, eliminates copy-paste bugs, simplifies adding rate limiting or logging consistently.
findings.risk: Low — mechanical refactor; behavior preserved if factory captures same logic.

findings.title: Dead code branch in every legacy-monolith handler — `if (!data)` never executes
findings.description: `data` is assigned the result of `ROUTES[cacheKey] || {…}`, which is always truthy (either cached object or newly created object). The `if (!data)` block is unreachable; the `else` branch always runs. The nested logic inside the dead branch (lines 7-18) is never executed.
findings.suggestion: Remove the dead `if (!data)` block and keep only the `else` branch (`res.json(data)`), or fix the logic if the intent was to check cache miss before assignment.
findings.benefit: Eliminates confusing dead code; may reveal intended cache-miss behavior.
findings.risk: Low if branch is truly dead; verify no side effects in the nested block (there are none — only res.json calls).

findings.title: save_config leaks file handle — no context manager
findings.description: If `fh.write(data)` raises an exception, `fh.close()` is never called, leaking a file descriptor. Should use `with open(path, 'w') as fh:`.
findings.snippet:
def save_config(path, data):
    fh = open(path, "w")
    fh.write(data)
    fh.close()
findings.suggestion: Rewrite as `with open(path, 'w') as fh: fh.write(data)`.
findings.benefit: Guarantees file closure on error; prevents descriptor exhaustion.
findings.risk: None — purely mechanical fix.

findings.title: Duplicate renderInvoice exported from both utils.js and helpers.js — namespace collision risk
findings.description: Identical renderInvoice function exists in both src/utils.js and src/helpers.js (lines 1-30 in both). Any consumer importing from both gets a collision; maintenance must update two copies.
findings.suggestion: Keep a single source of truth (e.g., utils.js) and re-export from helpers.js, or delete helpers.js's copy and use utils.js directly.
findings.benefit: Single maintenance point; avoids version skew.
findings.risk: Low — verify no subtle behavioral differences (there are none; code is identical).

findings.title: Dependency hygiene issues in package.json (3)
findings.description:
- **express** `latest`: production dependency pinned to "*" / "latest" — builds are non-reproducible
- **lodash** `*`: production dependency pinned to "*" / "latest" — builds are non-reproducible
- **lodash** `* / 4.17.21`: same package in dependencies and devDependencies
findings.suggestion: Pin exact versions (lockfiles for npm/cargo; `==` pins or constraints.txt for pip) and audit ranges deliberately when upgrading.
findings.benefit: Reproducible builds and no surprise breaking upgrades.
findings.risk: Low — pinning alone changes no runtime behavior.

modelVerdicts.reason: Dependencies use 'latest', '*', and duplicate lodash in prod+dev.

findings.title: No lockfile committed next to package.json
findings.description: Without a lockfile, every `npm install` resolves fresh versions — CI, teammates, and production can drift apart silently.
findings.suggestion: Commit the lockfile matching your package manager (npm/yarn/pnpm) and install with `npm ci` in CI.
findings.benefit: Identical dependency trees everywhere; fewer "works on my machine" failures.
findings.risk: None — adding a lockfile is additive.

modelVerdicts.reason: No package-lock.json or yarn.lock in repository summary.

findings.title: Import cycle (2 modules): a.js → b.js → a.js
findings.description: Circular import chain: src/lib/a.js → src/lib/b.js → src/lib/a.js. Cycles cause initialization-order bugs (undefined imports at runtime), prevent clean layering, and make the modules impossible to test in isolation.
findings.suggestion: Break the cycle by extracting the shared piece into a third module, or invert one dependency via dependency injection / event callbacks.
findings.benefit: Deterministic module initialization and clean layering.
findings.risk: Moderate — moving code between modules can shift initialization order; run the full test suite after.

modelVerdicts.reason: a.js requires './b.js'; summary confirms cycle a.js → b.js → a.js.
